stories.headline: Senate Impeachment Trial Postponed for Second Consecutive Day Amid Flooding
stories.deck: The second weather delay pushes the trial calendar further back as Metro Manila remains under emergency work arrangements.
body: The approved FMB News midday package reports that Presiding Officer Francis Escudero canceled the August 19 impeachment session, marking a second consecutive weather-related postponement.
The delay followed continuing monsoon flooding and the Palace directive shifting executive government work arrangements across NCR and several Luzon provinces.
Repeated postponements affect witness scheduling and the pace of a constitutional trial while prioritizing safe movement during severe weather.
Watch the Senate Impeachment Court for the Thursday session notice, witness lineup and any makeup-session adjustments.

stories.headline: DepEd Says 9,142 Schools Shifted to Distance Learning Amid Neneng, Habagat
stories.deck: The scale of the shift shows how prolonged severe weather is disrupting classroom instruction across Luzon.
body: The approved FMB News midday package reports that 9,142 public and private schools across Metro Manila and 17 Luzon provinces suspended in-person classes and activated Alternative Delivery Modes on August 19.
Alternative Delivery Modes can include printed modules and asynchronous or remote learning, depending on school capacity and local instructions.
Large-scale learning disruption can compound existing education gaps, making both safety and continuity planning important during extended weather emergencies.
Watch DepEd for updated school counts, return-to-class guidance, damage assessments and support for affected learners and teachers.

stories.headline: TD Neneng Tracks Toward Batanes as PAGASA Monitors Three Cyclonic Systems
stories.deck: The combined weather pattern keeps monsoon rains and gale conditions in focus for northern and western Luzon.
body: The approved FMB News overnight package, citing PAGASA, reports Tropical Depression Neneng moving west-northwestward toward waters near Batanes with sustained winds around 45 km/h and gusts up to 55 km/h.
Neneng's center was forecast to remain mainly over water, but the wider circulation of the systems was continuing to enhance the Southwest Monsoon.
Batanes, Babuyan and coastal communities face marine and rainfall risks even when a cyclone center does not make direct landfall.
Watch PAGASA for track changes, intensity updates, gale warnings and monsoon rainfall advisories.

stories.headline: Palace Extends Alternative Government Work to August 20 in NCR and 17 Provinces
stories.deck: The extension keeps flexible work arrangements in place as residual flood and transport risks continue.
body: The approved FMB News evening package reports that Malacañang extended alternative work arrangements for executive government offices in Metro Manila and 17 Luzon provinces for Thursday, August 20.
The covered areas mirror the previous day's broad emergency setup, while class suspensions continue to depend on education and local-government decisions.
The extension affects civil-service operations, commuting and access to public offices while authorities work to restore flooded transport routes.
Watch Palace, agency and LGU advisories for the return to regular on-site operations and any further school suspension announcements.

stories.headline: Impeachment Court Set to Reconvene for Day 17 With Cash-Advance Custodians
stories.deck: The planned resumption follows a weather-related delay and returns attention to financial records and custody of cash advances.
body: The approved FMB News 7:00 AM package reports that the Senate Impeachment Court was scheduled to resume Day 17 at 9:00 AM on August 19 after the previous day's weather postponement.
The testimony was part of an ongoing evidentiary process. Claims and interpretations advanced by either side are not treated as established facts unless supported by evidence accepted by the court.
Witness testimony about financial custody and documentation may affect how senator-judges assess disputed confidential-fund transactions.
Watch the Senate for the actual session status, witness appearances, cross-examination and evidentiary rulings.

stories.headline: Palace Suspends In-Person Classes, Shifts Government Work in NCR and 17 Provinces
stories.deck: The expanded directive covers 18 jurisdictions as continued Habagat rains keep flood and travel risks elevated.
body: The approved FMB News package reports that Malacañang suspended in-person classes and ordered alternative work arrangements for executive government offices in Metro Manila and 17 provinces for Wednesday, August 19.
The package says frontline health, disaster response, law enforcement, fire protection and vital utility services remained subject to on-site operational requirements.
The directive affects school attendance, commuting and government-office operations across a large part of Luzon during a continuing weather emergency.
Check Palace, agency, LGU and school notices for implementation details, private-sector guidance and the timing of normal on-site operations.
